color.$description: Semantic tier, LIGHT theme. Role-named tokens (surface, fg, border, accent, status) that ARE the public contract (BR-BW-TOK-001): names are stable, values are brand-overridable. This file holds the authored light values; semantic.dark.tokens.json holds the authored dark values (BR-BW-TOK-002: dark is authored, never derived from light). Both files define the SAME token names. Derived tokens carry their live color-mix expression in $extensions.bw.derived (emitted as the CSS value); $value stays the resolved default and the regression baseline (docs/DESIGN.md section 3).

surface-sunken.$description: 0.4.0 polish: deepened from the 98.5% mix (gray.50), which was indistinguishable from the white chrome; the canvas now lands on gray.100 so cards, header bands and zebra stripes separate.

fg-muted.$description: 0.4.0 polish: raised from the 56% mix (gray.500, borderline AA) for comfortable secondary-text contrast; measures 5.82:1 on surface and 5.26:1 on the deeper sunken canvas. A literal: the resolved L sits between ramp steps.

status-fg-ink.$description: brickwork#289 review round 2: the fixed dark-ink partner every X-fg (danger/success/warning/info) mixes toward. Deliberately NOT var(--bw-color-fg): fg is one of the seven load-bearing tokens BRANDING.md tells every brand to author, so a derivation that tracked fg would let an ordinary, documented fg override quietly break status-text contrast (the same AA trap #289 closed for --bw-color-surface, one token over). This token defaults to the same value as --bw-color-fg (gray.900) so the shipped X-fg ratios are unchanged, but it is a distinct name a brand does not touch when it authors fg: overriding fg alone leaves status-text contrast exactly where base-theme verified it. A brand wanting different status-text ink authors this token directly (rare) and re-verifies the contrastPairs pairings itself.

border-control.$description: Input/control boundary. The divider border token stays light for calm chrome; controls need a WCAG 1.4.11 compliant boundary (measured 3.23:1 against the default light surface).

accent-subtle.$description: Literal, not the blue.50 alias: the achromatic light surface is hue-powerless in the mix, so the resolved hue stays the accent's 262, not the ramp's 254.

danger-subtle.$description: Literal, not the red.50 alias: the achromatic surface is hue-powerless, so the resolved hue stays the danger base's 27, not the ramp's 18.

danger-border.$description: Tinted badge/alert border for the danger intent.

danger-fg.$description: brickwork#289: text on danger-subtle (and on plain surface: .bw-field__error, .bw-account-menu__item--danger). Was a fixed mix toward literal black, independent of --bw-color-surface; danger-subtle mixes toward surface, so a brand darkening surface closed the gap and dropped contrast below AA with no warning. brickwork#289 review round 2: mixing toward var(--bw-color-fg) traded that failure for an equivalent one under an --bw-color-fg override (fg is itself a documented, brand-authored token, BRANDING.md's load-bearing seven), so the mix now targets var(--bw-color-status-fg-ink), a dedicated token defaulting to the same gray.900 ink but never moved by an ordinary --bw-color-fg override. This keeps the SAME numeric floor as the var(--bw-color-fg) attempt (status-fg-ink defaults to that attempt's resolution) while closing the fg-override hole: verified >= 4.5:1 against both danger-subtle and plain surface for --bw-color-surface overridden anywhere down to L 0.94 (conservative; the measured worst-family crossing is L 0.9390), independent of any --bw-color-fg value. Not the red.700 alias: mixing toward status-fg-ink resolves a fractionally different hue than a pure-black mix. Robustness is one-directional: this pairing is NOT protected against overriding --bw-color-danger itself to an extreme lightness, which is out of scope for #289 (that failure mode is the fg-on-accent class, docs/BRANDING.md).

warning-subtle.$description: Literal, not the amber.50 alias: the achromatic surface is hue-powerless, so the resolved hue stays the warning base's 58, not the ramp's 95.

warning-border.$description: Tinted badge/alert border for the warning intent.

warning-fg.$description: brickwork#289: text on warning-subtle (and on plain surface: .bw-field__error, .bw-stat__trend). Was a fixed mix toward literal black, independent of --bw-color-surface; warning-subtle mixes toward surface, so darkening surface closed the gap and dropped contrast below AA (the reported defect: default was only 4.67, and any surface darker than L 0.986 failed). brickwork#289 review round 2: mixing toward var(--bw-color-fg) traded that failure for an equivalent one under an --bw-color-fg override, so the mix now targets var(--bw-color-status-fg-ink), a dedicated token defaulting to the same gray.900 ink but never moved by an ordinary --bw-color-fg override. Verified >= 4.5:1 against both warning-subtle and plain surface for --bw-color-surface overridden anywhere down to L 0.94 (conservative; measured worst-family crossing L 0.9390), independent of --bw-color-fg.

success-border.$description: Tinted badge/alert border for the success intent.

success-fg.$description: brickwork#289: text on success-subtle (and on plain surface: .bw-field__error, .bw-stat__trend). Was a fixed mix toward literal black, independent of --bw-color-surface; success-subtle mixes toward surface, so darkening surface closed the gap and dropped contrast below AA. brickwork#289 review round 2: mixing toward var(--bw-color-fg) traded that failure for an equivalent one under an --bw-color-fg override, so the mix now targets var(--bw-color-status-fg-ink), a dedicated token defaulting to the same gray.900 ink but never moved by an ordinary --bw-color-fg override. Verified >= 4.5:1 against both success-subtle and plain surface for --bw-color-surface overridden anywhere down to L 0.94 (conservative; measured worst-family crossing L 0.9390), independent of --bw-color-fg. Not the green.700 alias: mixing toward the ink literal resolves a fractionally different hue than a pure-black mix.

success-on-fg.$description: Near-black ink, the same treatment as warning: white on the solid green base fails AA (3.32); this ink measures 5.97.

info-subtle.$description: Literal, not the cyan.50 alias: the achromatic surface is hue-powerless, so the resolved hue stays the info base's 225, not the ramp's 210.

info-border.$description: Tinted badge/alert border for the info intent.

Verified >= 4.5:1 against both info-subtle and plain surface for --bw-color-surface overridden anywhere down to L 0.94 (conservative; measured worst-family crossing L 0.9390), independent of --bw-color-fg. Not the cyan.700 alias: mixing toward the ink literal resolves a fractionally different hue than a pure-black mix.

focus-ring.$description: brickwork#134: derived from accent, not a flat literal. A hardcoded amber broke brand-agnosticism: every white-label tenant would get an amber ring regardless of their brand accent, contradicting the overridable-manifest contract (this token was previously `derived: var(--bw-color-accent)`, which failed WCAG 1.4.11 at only 2.53:1 against surface). The fix keeps the accent's hue and mixes it toward black to force a contrast-safe lightness: 95% accent, 5% black, in oklab (never oklch, which rotates hue toward 0 on a tint mix). A tenant's `--bw-color-accent` still flows through as the ring's hue. Resolved literal for the default blue.600 accent, not an alias: clears 3:1 against every surface the ring is painted on (the global :focus-visible rule and the marketing hero/CTA bands) at surface/surface-raised 5.73:1 and surface-inverse (gray.900) 3.13:1.

nav-item-active-bg.$description: Follows accent-subtle's resolved literal (hue 262, not the blue.50 ramp's 254).

nav-section-text.$description: Follows fg-muted's resolved literal (0.4.0: the 62% mix).

skeleton-bg.$description: One step deeper than the sunken canvas so the placeholder reads as one. 0.4.0 polish: constant retuned 94% to 96% to hold the gray.200 landing above the deeper 96.5% sunken.

surface-marketing-tint.$description: 1.2.0 marketing token (BR-BW-MKT marketing tokens): a subtle tinted section background for marketing bands (_cta.html and any tinted section), derived from the accent/surface pair so a brand recolours it for free. Mixed at a low percentage (8%, one step past accent-subtle's 7%) so text placed on it clears WCAG AA in both themes (BR-BW-MKT-002's both-themes axe gate). Resolved literal (hue rotates toward the achromatic surface's own hue under oklab interpolation, unlike accent-subtle which mixes toward an achromatic-in-oklch literal), not an alias.

chart-axis.$description: Axis line and ticks. Authored per theme, never derived (CHT-005). Measures 7.44:1 on the default surface: an axis is a non-text graphical object and clears WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1.

chart-grid.$description: Gridlines. Deliberately low contrast (1.40:1) and deliberately NOT held to 3:1: a gridline is decoration that must recede behind the data, not a graphical object conveying information. The data series carry the meaning.

chart-axis-label.$description: Axis tick labels. Authored per theme (CHT-005), and deliberately DARKER than fg-muted's 0.507 rather than reusing it: fg-muted is tuned for body text and measures 4.37:1 on the base surface, which is below the 4.5:1 AA floor once the value is held to a text standard. Chart axis labels are small text on a card, so they are authored at 6.5:1 instead. Caught by test_axis_label_clears_the_text_contrast_floor, which did not exist when the value was first copied from fg-muted.

chart-tooltip-bg.$description: Chart tooltip background. Inverted against the light surface (the tooltip is a transient overlay, matching the package's inverse-surface convention).

chart-tooltip-text.$description: Chart tooltip text. Measures 17.2:1 on tooltip-bg, comfortably clear of AA for the small text a tooltip carries.

chart-tooltip-border.$description: Chart tooltip border: a subtle lift off the tooltip background, not a contrast affordance.

state.$description: Interactive-state tokens, LIGHT theme (DESIGN.md section 4.6). Transient feedback is a translucent overlay laid over whatever surface is beneath; persistent selection is a dedicated token. Theme-variant like color.*: same names in semantic.dark.tokens.json.

selected-bg.$description: Follows accent-subtle's resolved literal (hue 262, not the blue.50 ramp's 254).

elevation.$description: Elevation ramp, LIGHT theme (DESIGN.md section 5). Geometry adopted from Tailwind 4's shadow ramp, colours in oklch. Theme-variant: dark values are authored in semantic.dark.tokens.json (higher alpha plus an inset top highlight from level 3).
